'''Judea Pearl''' ({{Langx|he|יהודה פרל}}; born September 4, 1936) is an Israeli-American [[Electrical engineering|electrical engineer]], [[computer scientist]] and [[philosopher]], best known for championing the probabilistic approach to [[artificial intelligence]] and the development of [[Bayesian networks]] (see the article on [[belief propagation]]). He is also credited for developing a theory of causal and counterfactual inference based on structural models (see article on [[causality]]). In 2011, the [[Association for Computing Machinery]] (ACM) awarded Pearl with the [[Turing Award]], the highest distinction in computer science, "for fundamental contributions to artificial intelligence through the development of a calculus for probabilistic and causal reasoning".<ref name="acm-turing"/><ref name="acm_2011_Turing_award_ Judea_Pearl_press_release">{{cite web
 |author       = Gold, Virginia
 |title        = Judea Pearl Wins ACM A.M. Turing Award for Contributions that Transformed Artificial Intelligence
 |publisher    = The [[Association for Computing Machinery]]
 |date         = March 15, 2012
 |url          = http://www.acm.org/press-room/news-releases/2012/turing-award-11
 |access-date  = March 15, 2012
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20120317233913/http://www.acm.org/press-room/news-releases/2012/turing-award-11
 |archive-date = March 17, 2012
 |quote        = [[Association for Computing Machinery|ACM]], the [[Association for Computing Machinery]] today named Judea Pearl of the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] the winner of the 2011 ACM [[A.M. Turing Award]] for innovations that enabled remarkable advances in the partnership between humans and machines that is the foundation of [[Artificial Intelligence]] (AI).
 |url-status   = dead
}}</ref><ref name="acm">{{ACMPortal|id= 81548012093}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1109/MIC.2006.107| title = Judea Pearl Interview: A Giant of Artificial Intelligence Takes on All-Too-Real Hatred| journal = IEEE Internet Computing| volume = 10| issue = 5| pages = 6–8| year = 2006| last1 = Goth | first1 = G.| bibcode = 2006IIC....10e...6G| s2cid = 9932352}}</ref> He is the author of several books, including the technical ''[[Causality (book)|Causality: Models, Reasoning and Inference]]'', and ''[[The Book of Why]]'', a book on causality aimed at the general public.

Judea Pearl is the father of journalist [[Daniel Pearl]], who was kidnapped and murdered by terrorists in [[Pakistan]] connected with Al-Qaeda and the International Islamic Front in 2002.<ref name = "Time">{{cite magazine

==Biography==
Judea Pearl was born in [[Tel Aviv]], [[Israel]], in 1936 to Eliezer and Tova Pearl, who were [[History of Jews in Poland|Polish Jewish]] immigrants, grew up in [[Bnei Brak]]. His grandfather Chaim Pearl was one of Bnei Brak's founders.<ref>[https://jewishjournal.com/cover_story/341299/judea-pearl-reflections-on-loss-artificial-intelligence-and-zionophobia/ Judea Pearl: Reflections on Loss, Artificial Intelligence, and “Zionophobia”]</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.haaretz.com/jewish/2015-02-01/ty-article/.premium/this-day-in-history-daniel-pearl-murdered/0000017f-eb32-d639-af7f-ebf7a9040000|title = This Day in Jewish History / Journalist Daniel Pearl murdered in Pakistan by Islamic terrorists|newspaper = Haaretz}}</ref><ref>[https://jewishjournal.com/commentary/columnist/372736/the-audacious-joy-of-judea-pearl/ The Audacious Joy of Judea Pearl]</ref> He is a descendant of [[Menachem Mendel of Kotzk]] on his mother's side. After serving in the [[Israel Defense Forces]] and joining a [[kibbutz]], Pearl decided to study engineering in 1956. He received a B.S. in electrical engineering from the [[Technion]] 1960. That same year, he emigrated to the United States and pursued graduate studies. He received an M.S. in electrical engineering from the Newark College of Engineering (now [[New Jersey Institute of Technology]]) in 1961, and went on to receive an M.S. in physics from [[Rutgers University]] and a PhD in electrical engineering from the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn (now the [[New York University Tandon School of Engineering]]) in 1965.<ref name=amturing>{{Cite web|url=https://amturing.acm.org/award_winners/pearl_2658896.cfm|title=Judea Pearl – A.M. Turing Award Laureate|website=amturing.acm.org}}</ref> He worked at [[RCA Corporation#Diversification|RCA]] Research Laboratories (now [[SRI International]]) in [[Princeton, New Jersey]] on superconductive [[parametric amplifier]]s and storage devices and at Electronic Memories, Inc., on advanced memory systems.<ref name=amturing/> When [[semiconductor]]s "wiped out" Pearl's work, as he later expressed it,<ref name="cacm">{{cite journal |title=Q&A: A Sure Thing |author=Leah Hoffmann |journal=[[Communications of the ACM]] |volume=55 |number=6 |pages=135–136 |doi=10.1145/2184319.2184347 |year=2012|doi-access=free }}</ref> he joined [[UCLA]]'s [[Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science|School of Engineering]] in 1970 and started work on probabilistic [[artificial intelligence]]. He is one of the founding editors of the ''Journal of Causal Inference''.

Pearl is currently a professor of computer science and statistics and director of the Cognitive Systems Laboratory at UCLA. He and his wife, [[Ruth Pearl|Ruth]], had three children. In addition, {{As of|2011|lc=y}}, he is a member of the International Advisory Board of [[NGO Monitor]].<ref name = "NGO">{{cite web
|url         = http://www.ngo-monitor.org/article.php?viewall=yes&id=2028
|title       = International Advisory Board Profiles
|year        = 2011
|publisher   = [[NGO Monitor]]
|access-date = July 20, 2011
}}</ref>

Former Israeli Chief Rabbi, Rabbi [[Yisrael Meir Lau]], partnered with Judea Pearl in the documentary ''With My Whole Broken Heart''.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wilkinson|first1=Phaedra|title=From the community: With My Whole Broken Heart|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/deerfield/community/chi-ugc-article-with-my-whole-broken-heart-2015-07-10-story.html|agency=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=July 10, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|VoEjCnrppdw|With My Whole Broken Heart trailer}}</ref>

==Murder of Daniel Pearl==
In 2002, his son, [[Daniel Pearl]], a journalist working for the ''[[Wall Street Journal]]'' was kidnapped and murdered in [[Pakistan]], leading Judea and the other members of the family and friends to create the [[Daniel Pearl Foundation]].<ref name="DPF">{{cite web
 |url          = http://www.danielpearl.org/about_us/Judea_Pearl.html
 |title        = Biography of Dr. Judea Pearl
 |year         = 2011
 |publisher    = [[Daniel Pearl Foundation]]
 |access-date  = July 20, 2011
 |url-status   = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20110630070829/http://www.danielpearl.org/about_us/Judea_Pearl.html
 |archive-date = June 30, 2011
}}</ref> On the seventh anniversary of Daniel's death, Judea wrote an article in the ''Wall Street Journal'' titled ''Daniel Pearl and the Normalization of Evil: When will our luminaries stop making excuses for terror?''.<ref name = "WSJ">{{cite news
| title       = Daniel Pearl and the Normalization of Evil
| first       = Judea
| last        = Pearl
| author-link = Judea Pearl
| url         = https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB123362422088941893
| newspaper   = [[The Wall Street Journal]]
| date        = February 3, 2009
| page        = A15
| access-date = July 20, 2011
}}</ref>

Emeritus [[Chief Rabbi of the United Hebrew Congregations of Great Britain and the Commonwealth|Chief Rabbi]] [[Jonathan Sacks]] quoted Judea Pearl's beliefs in a lesson on [[Judaism]]: "I asked Judea Pearl, father of the murdered journalist Daniel Pearl, why he was working for reconciliation between Jews and Muslims...he replied with heartbreaking lucidity, "Hate killed my son. Therefore I am determined to fight hate."<ref>{{cite web|author1=Jonathan Sacks|title=Judaism: Covenant & Conversation: Against Hate|url=http://www.israelnationalnews.com/Articles/Article.aspx/15622|work=[[Israel National News]]|date=September 5, 2014}}</ref>

==Views==
On his religious views, Pearl states that he is a "practicing disbeliever."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.greatertalent.com/speaker-news/judea-pearl-history-has-given-us-both-a-tragedy-and-an-opportunity/|title=Tragedy and Opportunity: The parents of slain journalist Danny Pearl have devoted their lives to improving Muslim-Jewish relations.|access-date=July 12, 2013|author=Mathew Philips|quote=I turned secular at the age of 11, by divine revelation. [Laughs.] I was standing on the roof of the house my father built, looking down on the street and suddenly it became very clear to me that there is no God.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Robots and the Illusion of Free Will – Conversation with Judea Pearl, Rumelhart Prize Winner|work=The Science Network |url=http://thesciencenetwork.org/programs/cogsci-2011/interview-with-judea-pearl|location=|date=July 22, 2011|quote=I'm, of course, prisoner of my upbringing, which means my store of metaphors comes from the Bible and comes from history of the Jewish people. But I don't believe in God. Actually, I know there isn't [a] God.}}</ref> He is very connected to Jewish traditions such as holidays and [[kiddush]] on Friday night.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Fishman Orlins|first1=Susan|title=The Price of Being Jewish: An Interview with Judea Pearl|url=http://www.momentmag.com/the-price-of-being-jewish-an-interview-with-judea-pearl/|agency=Moment|date=November 2006|quote=Did you pray for Danny’s safe return? No, I don't believe in a God [that] would listen to me. But I do pray every morning. I lay tefillin. I started a year ago. But aren’t you a secular Jew? I'll give you the same answer I gave 10 Muslims who joined me for dinner one Friday night. I said, 'Oh, it's Friday night. I have to do Kiddush.'}}</ref>

Pearl sits on the [[NGO Monitor]] international advisory board<ref>{{Cite web |title=International Advisory Board |url=https://ngo-monitor.org/about/boards/#IAB |access-date=June 27, 2025 |website=NGO Monitor}}</ref>, a right-wing organization based in Jerusalem that reports on [[non-governmental organization]] activity from a pro-Israel perspective.

==Research==
Pearl is credited for "laying the foundations of modern artificial intelligence, so computer systems can process  uncertainty and relate causes to effects."
<ref name="bbva" />
He is one of the pioneers of [[Bayesian networks]] and the [[probability|probabilistic]] approach to [[artificial intelligence]], and one of the first to mathematize causal modeling in the empirical sciences. His work is also intended as a high-level [[cognitive model]]. He is interested in the [[philosophy of science]], [[knowledge representation]], [[nonclassical logic|nonstandard logic]]s, and learning. Pearl is described as "one of the giants in the field of artificial intelligence" by UCLA computer science professor [[Richard E. Korf]].<ref name ="Korf">{{cite journal
| last1       = Amundson
| first1      = Marlys
| date        = Fall 2004
| title       = A Profile of Judea Pearl – Computer Science Pioneer, Visionary
| journal     = UCLA Engineer
| issue       = 12
| pages       = 16–17
| access-date = July 20, 2011
| url         = http://ftp.cs.ucla.edu/pub/stat_ser/pearl-engineer-fall04.pdf
}}</ref> His work on [[causality#Causal calculus|causality]] has "revolutionized the understanding of causality in statistics, psychology, medicine and the social sciences" according to the [[Association for Computing Machinery]].<ref name = "ACM">{{cite web
|url         = http://bayes.cs.ucla.edu/Newell_2003.htm
|title       = ACM HONORS INNOVATORS WHO CHANGED THE SCIENTIFIC WORLD
|date        = April 27, 2004 |publisher = [[Association for Computing Machinery]]
|location    = [[New York City|New York]]
|access-date = July 20, 2011
}}</ref>

===Notable contributions===
* A summary of Pearl's scientific contributions is available in a chronological [http://amturing.acm.org/award_winners/pearl_2658896.cfm account] authored by [[Stuart J. Russell]] (2012). 
* An [http://amturing.acm.org/bib/pearl_2658896.cfm annotated bibliography] of Pearl's contributions was compiled by the ACM in 2012.
* A video describing Pearl's major contributions to AI is available [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uaq389ckd5o here].
* Pearl's opinion pieces, touching on Jewish identity, the war on terrorism, and the Middle East conflict can be accessed [http://bayes.cs.ucla.edu/Judea-Pearl-Op-eds.pdf here].
